notes: Lattice-square variety trial of 49 soybeans in 4 reps (Weiss & Cox 1939). Help fits a fixed lm/asreml yield ~ rep + rep:col + rep:row + gen (matching Weiss table 7). Mixed rendering treats the incomplete row/column blocks within rep as random, rep and genotype fixed; rep:col and rep:row are composites built from their parts. rep is a design factor by the five-level rule: four reps (R1 to R4), fitted as fixed in the help's lm and asreml calls.

formula: cbind(r, n - r) ~ x + block + (1 | var)
notes: boot help: randomized block design, 45 sugar-cane varieties x 4 blocks, diseased shoots r out of total shoots n (binomial); no model fitted. Rendered as random-effects GLMM per Census block-design rule; variety random (aim is to classify the 45 varieties by resistance), block fixed, x (stem pieces planted) a covariate. block is a design factor by the five-level rule: four blocks (A to D), described in words only and fitted as random by no cited source. Retained var assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger cultivar population; this remains unverified.

Read Spruce.Rd (App. A.28; Diggle et al. 1994 Ex. 1.3); the page gives no model, and the ozone treatment is not a column. Tree codes (O1T01) encode the plot, so Tree is nested in plot. plot has four levels, but the lmeSplines examples (smspline, manual p.5) fit random plot and Tree intercepts on logSize ~ days with a smoothing spline in days; this formula simplifies that spline model to a linear time trend.

Hand sample #61: a split-plot field trial (the 4e data), y the yield, N (nitrogen, five levels) the whole-plot and G (genotype, two levels) the subplot treatment, row and column crossed blocks, row:col the whole plot.
